Pebble Works to confirm internal security contact and add to thread by 2026-01-20
Schedule technical deep dive for private deployment (SE-led) week of 2026-01-26

Ari Soto: confirm VPC peering window and provide network diagram - due 2026-01-20

summary: Kickoff for sprint-zero and infra intake. Agreed to run a private deployment proof-of-connection in staging, validate latency and token throughput, and align on security/SSO/KMS needs. Identified a 3-week runway for initial pilot with a follow-up deep dive on federation and tenancy.
topics: Throughput & latency benchmarks for production prompts
questions: Does Redwood support customer-managed HSM for key storage?
How does automatic KV cache warming behave on model rollouts?
What is the fallback policy if Dedicated capacity hits quota?
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-01-18 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood), Ethan (Redwood SE), Jules (Redwood Impl), Ari (Pebble Works), Devon (Pebble Infra), Samira (Pebble PM)

Summary block (auto): agreed sprint-zero scope, collect network details, schedule deep technical test.

00:00 Maya Thornton: okay everyone good, we'll give it a minute for folks to join, umhh, thanks for making time.
00:18 Ari Soto: yeah thanks, Ari from Pebble Works, happy to be here. we've got Devon and Samira with me.
00:28 Ethan Patel: hi folks, ethan here, i'll be owning the bench plan and the SE side of the runbook. quick note, i'm on pacific time so apologies if i blurt in early.
00:40 Jules Kim: jules from implementation, i'll manage the sprint-zero milestones.
00:52 Samira Rahman: hey, samira, product - i've got questions about eval criteria - latency thresholds and quality metrics.
01:10 Maya Thornton: perfect, the agenda we sent: network intake, sso/keys, bench plan, and success criteria. feel free to call out if anything missing.
01:33 Ari Soto: sounds good. quick context: we run a multi-tenant orchestration, our infra is mostly aws in us-west-2, some eu workloads; need private tenancy for sensitive flows. timeline is aggressive — pilot in 3 weeks if possible.
01:58 Devon Blake: and we have strict audit needs — SOC2 in progress, need audit logs and SSO across teams. also we use Hashi vault for keys today.
02:26 Ethan Patel: okay great. on the vault/hsm front: redwood supports KMS integrations, and we have a private key-handoff pattern for private deployments. full HSM customer-managed is something we can integrate but needs a short policy review — i'll flag that as an engineering check. (slight pause) also, just to set expectations, benching for throughput vs latency tradeoffs can vary depending on model quantization and sequence length.
03:05 Samira Rahman: when you say "benching" — what does the bench plan look like? typical tokens/sec, tail latency p95?
03:18 Ethan Patel: good q. plan we'll propose: representative prompt set (you provide), 50 concurrent sessions ramped, measure p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens estimate. also measure cold-start vs warmed KV cache.
03:38 Ari Soto: ok we'll prep prompts. question: we default to private deployment in a VPC, what's the peering pattern? do you require direct peering or transit?
03:56 Jules Kim: we recommend VPC peering when feasible, but if customers use transit or VPN that's supported. we sent a VPC checklist — i'll resend. peering has lower latency but requires routing updates.
04:18 Devon Blake: important: we can't open wide egress to redwood managed services, company policy. are there options for a customer-controlled connector?
04:34 Ethan Patel: yes, there's an agent-style connector for on-prem or private cloud customers. in our private deployment we can run the control plane in your VPC or provide a private endpoint. it's a config choice.
04:52 Ari Soto: cool. on SSO — we use Okta, want SAML and role mappings to our internal teams. how granular is RBAC?
05:08 Maya Thornton: we support SAML SSO and can map to RBAC roles. default roles are admin, engineer, auditor; we can add custom roles. for compliance, audit logs are exportable to your SIEM.
05:28 Samira Rahman: do audit logs include token-level request traces? we need to show which user invoked what prompt.
05:40 Jules Kim: audit logs include request metadata and user identity, not raw prompt contents by default — we can discuss retention policies. if you need full prompt retention for debugging, that's configurable but has compliance implications.
06:05 Devon Blake: okay noted. back to keys: we use Hashi vault. is there an out-of-the-box integration?
06:15 Ethan Patel: yes, we have a Hashi Vault connector for secrets and we support external KMS via API. for HSM we need a short security review — i'll put that in the action items.
06:32 Ari Soto: great. next on benching: what about model variants — we might want cheaper quantized models for non-sensitive flows. how do rollouts look?
06:45 Ethan Patel: we support model rollouts and auto-fallbacks. rollout policy can be canary, a/b, or percentage based. note that quantized variants may slightly change output tokenization and occasionally quality; we'll include quality regression checks.
07:10 Samira Rahman: ok so success criteria should include both latency p95 and a quality pass rate. we'll draft acceptance tests.
07:26 Maya Thornton: suggested pilot acceptance: p95 < 350ms for core flows, cost target x% below baseline, and quality pass >= 92% on curated eval set. open to tweak.
07:46 Ari Soto: 350ms p95 feels tight for long sequences; can we scope core flows to short context only?
07:58 Ethan Patel: yes scope to typical sequences. we'll capture distribution of lengths from your product team.
08:12 Devon Blake: about networking — i'll share a network diagram. also need to know what ports and IP ranges to open.
08:22 Jules Kim: i'll attach the exact port list and ephemeral IP ranges. we try to keep IP lists minimal for peering.
08:36 Samira Rahman: any gotchas for data residency? we have EU customers and need data to stay in eu-west-1 for that tenant. can you pin regions?
08:49 Maya Thornton: absolutely. you can pin model routing by region or tenant. we'll document region pinning and routing policies.
09:05 Ari Soto: timeline check: we want an initial staging smoke test by 2026-02-05, and production pilot two weeks after that. is that realistic?
09:17 Maya Thornton: yes that's within a 3-week runway if we get network access and prompts this week.
09:28 Ethan Patel: i'll need sample prompts, network access, and an account for perf generation. also prefer to run an initial 24h soak with a ramp to catch autoscaling behavior.
09:45 Devon Blake: soak test is fine but we need to limit anonymized data only.
09:55 Jules Kim: noted, redact PII and we can share a template for anonymization.
10:10 Samira Rahman: let's talk about rollback and incident runbooks briefly, who owns on-call during the pilot?
10:21 Maya Thornton: Redwood provides an on-call SE during the pilot window and we assign a CSM (me) for coordination. for Dedicated we can set a joint runbook and escalation matrix.
10:34 Ari Soto: do you provide SLAs for Dedicated?
10:41 Maya Thornton: yes dedicated capacity comes with SLA options, we'll include standard uptime and latency SLOs in the contract addendum.
10:50 Samira Rahman: legal will want specifics — i'll need the SLA doc.
10:56 Maya Thornton: i'll attach SLA and support matrix after this call.
11:05 Ari Soto: question about metrics: can you stream traces to our Datadog?
11:12 Ethan Patel: yes we have exporters for Datadog and Prometheus. traces and metrics can be forwarded to your telemetry.
11:20 Devon Blake: one more infra Q — do you run GPUs in the customer VPC or in your managed fleet?
11:28 Ethan Patel: in private deployments we can either bring the runtime into your VPC (you supply nodes) or host in our dedicated fleet with a private endpoint. bringing runtime into your VPC gives you more control but increases operational overhead for you.
11:46 Ari Soto: ok we prefer control for compliance.
11:52 Maya Thornton: understood. let's capture decisions: customer-controlled runtime in VPC for pilot.
12:00 Samira Rahman: who will configure SAML assertions? us or Redwood?
12:07 Jules Kim: typically customer configures Okta and we provide metadata; we'll do a joint test.
12:16 Ari Soto: good. can we see a sample runbook for incident triage?
12:22 Maya Thornton: yes i'll share a runbook template.
12:30 Ethan Patel: coming back to perf — a note: KV cache warm can dramatically reduce p95 for repeated prompts. cold-starts for long contexts can be costly. we'll include warm and cold tests.
12:48 Devon Blake: how do you handle secrets in logs? we cannot allow secrets to leak to your managed control plane.
12:56 Jules Kim: logs are redacted by default; we don't store raw secrets. for private deployments with runtime in your VPC all logs can be routed to your SIEM without leaving your network.
13:14 Samira Rahman: sounds good.
13:22 Ari Soto: okay next steps recap?
13:28 Maya Thornton: recap: 1) Redwood sends VPC checklist, SLA doc, runbook template, and port/IP list by tomorrow (2026-01-19). 2) Pebble Works to provide network diagram, Okta admin contact, and sample prompt set by 2026-01-20. 3) SE to send perf plan by 2026-01-25. 4) schedule deep-dive week of 2026-01-26.
13:55 Devon Blake: confirmed.
14:02 Samira Rahman: hey small thing — are there pre-built plugins for our data connectors?
14:08 Ethan Patel: we have a few connectors for common stores; if not we can prototype in sprint-zero.
14:17 Ari Soto: ok good. any competitor considerations? legal asked about Bedrock integration and OpenAI fallback cost modeling.
14:30 Maya Thornton: we can provide a cost-compare sheet; note Bedrock is an option but doesn't give the same op controls for private deployments.
14:42 Samira Rahman: thanks.
14:48 Maya Thornton: any final questions?
14:52 Devon Blake: none from infra.
15:00 Ari Soto: no more from us. thanks, appreciate it.
15:06 Maya Thornton: great, i'll follow up with the docs and action items. thanks everyone.
15:15 [meeting ended]
